copyPanel.formula: Area = ½ × Base × Height (A = ½ b · h)
steps: 1. Identify the base and the perpendicular height to that base
2. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
3. Multiply base by height, then divide by 2

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
revealWordProblem.text: The front of this A-frame cabin is a triangle with a base of 34 ft and a height of 23¾ ft. Find the area of the triangular front that needs to be painted.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A photograph of an A-frame cabin with its triangular front outlined, labeled 34 feet across the base and 23 and three-fourths feet for the height.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 34 × 23¾. First, 23¾ = 23.75, so 34 × 23.75 = 807.5. Then take half: 807.5 ÷ 2 = 403.75. The triangular front of the cabin has an area of 403.75 square feet.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: 16 comes from adding 10 + 6. Area means multiply the base and height, then take half.
The number is right, but cm measures length. Area needs square units (sq cm).
60 is base × height — the full rectangle. A triangle is half of that, so multiply by ½.
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 10 cm y altura de 6 cm?
questions.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 centímetros cuadrados.
hintsEs: Tienes una base de 10 cm y una altura de 6 cm: un triángulo solo necesita esas dos, más un paso especial.
Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo: usa A = ½ × b × h. Si solo multiplicas, tu respuesta sale al doble.
Multiplica 10 × 6 y luego saca la mitad del producto. Las unidades de área son centímetros cuadrados.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: 3 is 24 ÷ 8 — but that skips the ½. Double the area first: 2 × 24 = 48, then divide by the base.
12 is half of 24 — that divides by 2 instead of doubling. Try 2 × 24 = 48, then ÷ 8.
16 comes from 24 − 8. Use h = (2 × area) ÷ base instead of subtracting.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.
questions.stemEs: Un triángulo tiene un área de 24 sq ft y una base de 8 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el área (24 pies²) y la base (8 pies): estás despejando la altura al revés.
Simplifica primero: ½ × 8 = 4, así que la ecuación se vuelve 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 entre 4 para hallar la altura en pies.

questions.stem: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
questions.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.
choiceFeedback: The height is perpendicular to them.
hints: Think about drawing a diagonal across a rectangle — what two shapes does it create?
Compare a triangle to a rectangle with the same base and height. How much of the rectangle does the triangle cover?
Sketch a rectangle, draw one diagonal, and shade one triangle. What fraction of the rectangle did you shade?
questions.stemEs: ¿Por qué dividimos entre 2 al hallar el área de un triángulo?
questions.explanationEs: Un triángulo con base b y altura h cabe dentro de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura. El triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo, así que A = ½ × b × h.
choicesEs: Un triángulo es exactamente la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura
La base siempre es el doble de la altura
Siempre dividimos entre 2 las fórmulas de área
hintsEs: Piensa en trazar una diagonal en un rectángulo: ¿qué dos figuras se forman?
Compara un triángulo con un rectángulo de la misma base y altura. ¿Qué parte del rectángulo cubre el triángulo?

reviewHighlights.formula: Area = ½ × Base × Height (A = ½ b · h)
steps: 1. Identify the base and the perpendicular height to that base
2. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is forgetting the ½ — students multiply base × height like a rectangle and stop there, or they use the triangle's slanted side instead of the perpendicular height that's already given. Always check: did I take half, and did I use the straight-up height, not the slanted side?

level3.prompt: A rectangle is 12 ft by 8 ft. A diagonal line cuts it into two triangles. What is the area of each triangle? Explain how the triangle area formula relates to the rectangle area formula.
level3.sentenceFrame: The rectangle's area is ___ because ___. Each triangle's area is ___ because a diagonal splits a rectangle into ___ equal triangles, so A = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___.
level3.hint: Write the formula with given numbers; solve step by step.
hints: Start with the rectangle: its area comes from 12 × 8. The diagonal splits that area into two identical pieces.
Each triangle keeps the same base (12) and height (8) as the rectangle — so its area is half the rectangle's.
Compute 12 × 8, halve it for one triangle, then check with ½ × 12 × 8. Explain why both paths give the same number.
level3.explanation: The rectangle's area is 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, and one diagonal cuts it into two identical triangles, so each triangle is 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. The formula says the same thing: each triangle keeps the rectangle's base of 12 and height of 8, and A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. The ½ in the triangle formula IS that diagonal cut.
level3.explanationEs: El área del rectángulo es 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, y una diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos idénticos, así que cada triángulo mide 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. La fórmula dice lo mismo: cada triángulo conserva la base de 12 y la altura de 8 del rectángulo, y A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. El ½ de la fórmula del triángulo ES ese corte diagonal.
level3.promptEs: Un rectángulo mide 12 pies por 8 pies. Una línea diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos. ¿Cuál es el área de cada triángulo? Explica cómo se relaciona la fórmula del área del triángulo con la del rectángulo.
hintsEs: Empieza con el rectángulo: su área sale de 12 × 8. La diagonal parte esa área en dos piezas idénticas.
Cada triángulo conserva la misma base (12) y altura (8) del rectángulo, así que su área es la mitad de la del rectángulo.
Calcula 12 × 8, sácale la mitad para un triángulo y luego comprueba con ½ × 12 × 8. Explica por qué ambos caminos dan el mismo número.
